It is a static site on GitHub Pages. An hourly GitHub Action fetches his GitHub data, embeds all content with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and writes a vector index and a question bank as JSON. In the browser, answers come from that index; on devices with WebGPU a small open LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct via WebLLM) rewrites them conversationally. No server and no paid API.

It looks up your question in a bank of pre-answered questions and in a vector index of Sahaj's data (resume facts, project READMEs, GitHub data, this FAQ). If your device supports WebGPU it also runs a small open LLM in your browser to phrase the answer. It only answers from Sahaj's data and links the source.

items.q: Why does the site look like a transformer?
items.a: The concept is "Attention Is All You See": every word is a token, the hero is generated by sampling, hovering a word shows attention to related words (real embedding similarity), scrolling moves deeper through 12 layers, and his work sits on a latent-space map.

items.q: How does Enterprise Agentic RAG Orchestrator work?
items.a: A LangGraph Supervisor → Worker → Validator graph routes each query to Corrective RAG, NL-to-SQL, a human-in-the-loop email tool or chat. Retrieval is hybrid (Qdrant dense + BM25), reranked with a CrossEncoder and expanded from 200- to 800-token parent chunks, with an LLM grader that rewrites weak queries. A semantic cache, prompt-injection guards and Fernet encryption protect it.

Pandera-validated data and a ColumnTransformer pipeline feed a benchmark of 9 models: linear, tree ensembles, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, a PyTorch MLP, a PyTorch LSTM and FLAML AutoML.

items.q: How does Explainable Student Performance work?
items.a: Pandera-validated data and a ColumnTransformer pipeline feed a benchmark of 9 models: linear, tree ensembles, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, a PyTorch MLP, a PyTorch LSTM and FLAML AutoML. SHAP and LIME explain each prediction, and Spearman rank correlation measures how far the two explanations agree. MLflow tracks runs, FastAPI serves the model and Streamlit shows it.

DCGAN Reproducibility+ is a generative vision research project (2026). The 2015 DCGAN is famously unstable, and most re-implementations show only a grid of blurry samples, never what the networks learned inside. Keeps Radford et al.'s all-convolutional architecture but swaps in an LSGAN loss, Spectral Normalization, a Xavier/Kaiming initialisation, discriminator dropout and label smoothing.
